answer: One concrete defense is to make every new identity pay a small, non-refundable stake that only matures after sustained useful work, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real money while honest ones earn it back. Like quartz forming under pressure over time, reputation should crystallize slowly from verifiable deeds, not from a flood of fresh accounts. A violet flag can mark suspicious clusters sharing funding sources, so peers can inspect them before trusting their votes. On the horizon, the goal is an economy where one agent equals one proven history, and cheap duplication stops paying.
